name: AI workflow automation
short: The copy-paste work between your tools, done automatically: leads into the CRM, invoices matched, reports sent.
audience: Teams where someone still copies details from one tool into another: enquiries into the CRM, bills into the books, numbers into a weekly report.

automations.name: Lead capture to CRM
automations.text: Every enquiry from your website, ads and inbox lands in the CRM with its source filled in, and the right person is told at once.

automations.name: Invoice and receipt matching
automations.text: Bills are read, matched to the bank line and queued for approval. Only the odd ones reach a person.

automations.name: New client onboarding
automations.text: A signed form creates the folder, the tasks, the welcome email and the first invoice.

automations.name: Quote and invoice chasing
automations.text: Open quotes and unpaid invoices get a polite reminder on a schedule you set, and stop the moment someone replies.

automations.name: Weekly report, sent for you
automations.text: The numbers are pulled from your tools every Monday and sent as one short email.

deliverables: The working automation, built in your own n8n, Make or Zapier account
A one-page map of what starts it and which tools it touches
An alert when a step fails, with the failed item kept so it can be retried
A short video walkthrough for your team

mock.title: New enquiry to notified owner
mock.note: Illustrative workflow. Yours is drawn around the tools you already use.

name: AI agents and chatbots
short: An assistant on your website, WhatsApp or inbox that answers, qualifies and books, then hands over to a person when it should.
audience: Businesses that answer the same questions all day, on the website, in the inbox or on WhatsApp, and lose the enquiries that arrive after hours.

automations.name: Website chat that qualifies
automations.text: It asks the three or four questions you would ask, then books a call or passes the enquiry to you.

automations.name: Inbox triage and draft replies
automations.text: Incoming email is sorted and a reply is drafted in your voice. A person approves it before it goes.

automations.name: Answers from your own documents
automations.text: It answers from your price list, policies and FAQs, and says so when it does not know.

automations.name: Handover to a person
automations.text: When someone asks for a human, is upset, or asks something outside the rules, your team gets the whole conversation.

automations.name: Quiet-lead follow-up
automations.text: People who went quiet get a check-in. It stops when they reply or opt out.

deliverables: The agent running on your channels, under your accounts
Written rules: what it may answer alone and what it must hand over
A conversation log you can read at any time
A monthly review of the questions it could not answer

timeline.note: Including a week of supervised replies

Thanks. A property manager can call you tomorrow. Is 10:30 or 2:00 better?
Booked for 10:30 tomorrow. A confirmation is on its way by email, and the manager has your details.

name: Voice and WhatsApp receptionists
short: Every call and message answered day and night. Appointments booked, reminders sent, urgent cases passed to your team.
audience: Clinics, brokerages and service firms that miss calls while the front desk is busy or closed, and whose customers would rather send a message.

automations.name: Missed-call text-back
automations.text: A caller who does not get through gets a message within a minute, offering to book or to ask their question.

automations.name: Call answering and booking
automations.text: A voice agent picks up, answers the common questions, books into your calendar and takes a message for the rest.

automations.name: Appointment reminders
automations.text: A WhatsApp or text reminder with a one-tap confirm or reschedule. Freed slots go back into the diary.

automations.name: Patient and client recall
automations.text: People due a check-up, a review or a renewal get a message and a way to book.

automations.name: Urgent-case handover
automations.text: Anything that sounds urgent goes to a named person by call or message straight away.

deliverables: A phone number or WhatsApp Business line registered in your name
Scripts and rules you have approved, including what it must never say
Bookings written straight into your calendar or practice system
A daily summary of calls, bookings and handovers

timeline.note: Including WhatsApp Business approval and test calls

startsFrom.note: For a WhatsApp receptionist. Voice lines are scoped as custom.

messages.text: Hi, this is the reception assistant at the clinic. We missed your call just now. Would you like to book, or do you have a question?
We have Tuesday at 9:15 or Thursday at 8:30. Which suits you?
You are booked for Thursday at 8:30. A reminder will come the day before. Reply CHANGE to move it.

name: Meeting intelligence
short: Call notes written for you, the CRM updated, and the follow-up email drafted before you have left the meeting.
audience: Sales teams, agencies and advisers who spend the hour after every call writing notes, updating the CRM and drafting the follow-up.

automations.name: Call notes written for you
automations.text: Decisions, objections and next steps, set out in the template you already use.

automations.name: CRM updated after each call
automations.text: The deal stage, contact notes and tasks are filled in without anyone typing them.

automations.name: Follow-up email drafted
automations.text: A reply that reflects what was agreed, waiting in your drafts for you to approve.

automations.name: Action items to your task tool
automations.text: Each promise made on the call becomes a task with an owner and a date.

automations.name: Weekly pipeline digest
automations.text: What moved, what stalled, and which promised follow-ups are overdue.

deliverables: A notetaker connected to your calendar and meeting tools
A recording notice on every call, and a rule for meetings that are never recorded
Note and email templates matched to how you already write
A CRM field mapping that you sign off before it goes live

timeline.note: For one team and one CRM

name: AI audit
short: A free 30-minute review of one process. You get a costed plan showing what to automate first and what it should return.
audience: Owners who suspect something could be automated but do not want to buy a project to find out. You bring one slow, repetitive process. No preparation is needed.

agenda.title: You pick one process
agenda.text: The job that eats the most time, and who does it today.

agenda.title: We walk through it step by step
agenda.text: Where it starts, which tools it touches, where it stalls and how often it runs.

agenda.title: We put numbers on it
agenda.text: Hours a week, what an hour costs you, and what a mistake or a missed enquiry costs.

agenda.title: You hear a straight answer
agenda.text: Whether it is worth automating, roughly what it would cost, and what happens next. If it is not worth it, we say so.

planContents: The process as it runs today, drawn as a simple map
The one automation to build first, and why that one
A fixed setup fee and monthly retainer for it
The third-party tools it needs and what they are likely to cost you
The expected return, worked from your own numbers, with every assumption written down
What could go wrong, and how each risk is handled
A pilot plan: the scope, the timeline and how we will both judge it
deliverables: The written plan as a PDF, yours to keep and to take to anyone else
One email with the plan. No sales calls after it unless you ask
